value: complement obligatorily introduced by pour
the relative pronoun after pour is lequel/laquelle (le client pour lequel je travaille)

evidence.notes: Source example 'C'est le client pour lequel je travaille' shows pour + person and the lequel relative form. Confidence high.

value: en + present participle shares its subject with the main verb
the present participle is invariable in this construction

evidence.notes: Usage note states the person who arrives is also the person who calls; en + participe présent is invariable. Confidence high.

value: complement obligatorily introduced by à
not constructed with a direct object, unlike English call

evidence.notes: Usage note states téléphoner requires à before the person called; source example 'Téléphone à Jérôme immédiatement!'. Confidence high.

value: invariable
comparative formed with plus: plus tôt

evidence.notes: Adverb of time, invariable; plus tôt is the standard comparative. Confidence high.

value: complement obligatorily introduced by de before the infinitive
used in the imparfait to describe an action that had just happened

evidence.notes: Source explanation covers the immediate past in the imparfait with venir de + infinitive. Confidence high.

value: no preposition between venir and the dependent infinitive
à la maison is the fixed phrase for at home

evidence.notes: Source text 'venir manger à la maison ce soir' shows direct infinitive after venir and the fixed à la maison phrase. Confidence high.

value: complement obligatorily introduced by pour
the complement is a person or party, not a thing

evidence.notes: Source example 'Vous avez voté pour moi' shows pour + person. Confidence high on the preposition, moderate on the person restriction.

value: followed by an infinitive without a preposition
the passé composé of vouloir expresses a specific past refusal

evidence.notes: Source explanation states that when would refers to a specific action in the past the passé composé of vouloir is used. Confidence high.

value: followed by an infinitive without a preposition
the conditional form je voudrais is used for polite requests

evidence.notes: Source text includes 'Je voudrais vous parler' with vouloir + infinitive; conditional politeness is standard. Confidence high.

value: y is an obligatory part of the idiom
the possessive changes with the person: du mien, du tien, du sien, du nôtre, du vôtre, du leur

evidence.notes: Usage note lists the full possessive paradigm and the source example shows obligatory y (si elle n'y met pas du sien). Confidence high.
